hero.title: A financial system that works for Ethiopia’s people and economy
hero.lead: FSD Ethiopia finds what holds the country’s financial markets back, then works with regulators, policymakers and market actors to fix it, through technical assistance, grants and research.

about.title: Who we are
about.body: Launched in 2022 with funding from UK aid and the Gates Foundation, FSD Ethiopia builds on the work of FSD Africa. We identify the underlying causes of financial system failures and help market actors address them.
about.vision: Our vision is a thriving financial system that delivers real value to the broader economy and the people of Ethiopia.

work.title: Our work
work.intro: Three programme areas, each aimed at a constraint that keeps people and businesses outside the formal financial system.

fi.summary: We expand access to digital and traditional financial services, support reforms that digitise and open up finance, and deepen services for groups the market underserves, starting with women.
fi.f1: Refreshing the National Financial Inclusion Strategy for 2026–2030 with the National Bank of Ethiopia
fi.f2: Expanding digital payment agent networks under the national strategy
fi.f3: Increasing women’s use of digital financial services

ac.summary: We help businesses reach long-term finance and working capital, and help build the capital market institutions that make this possible.
ac.f1: Wider finance options for micro, small and medium enterprises: equity, bonds, microloans and working capital
ac.f2: Support to the Ethiopian Securities Exchange, including a crowd-investment platform and the ESX Academy
ac.f3: Interest-free financial market instruments, with the National Bank of Ethiopia

cf.summary: We help mobilise domestic and international capital for climate adaptation and mitigation, and build the instruments to channel it.
cf.f1: An annual Climate Finance Summit; the second was held in Addis Ababa in March 2026
cf.f2: A scoping study of green, social and sustainability bonds for the Ethiopian Capital Market Authority
cf.f3: Membership of the Global Islamic Climate Finance Alliance

boards.title: Women leading Ethiopia’s financial boards
boards.body: Women hold {banks}% of board seats in Ethiopia’s commercial banks. Capital market rules now ask securities issuers to reach at least {ecma}%. Our Board Ready Program, run with IFC, prepares women professionals for those seats.
boards.tableCaption: Women’s share of board seats compared with the regulatory minimum
boards.programmeBody: Three cohorts have completed corporate governance training covering board roles and responsibilities, ESG principles and board-level decision-making.
boards.quoteBy: Programme graduate, name to be confirmed
